####
[SteamVR_Action_Skeleton_Source](Valve.VR.SteamVR_Action_Skeleton_Source.html)

Skeleton Actions are our best approximation of where your hands are while
holding vr controllers and pressing buttons. We give you 31 bones to help you
animate hand models. For more information check out this blog post:
<https://steamcommunity.com/games/250820/announcements/detail/1690421280625220068>

[SteamVR_ActivateActionSetOnLoad](Valve.VR.SteamVR_ActivateActionSetOnLoad.html)

#### [SteamVR_Behaviour_Boolean](Valve.VR.SteamVR_Behaviour_Boolean.html)

This component simplifies using boolean actions.

Provides editor accessible events: OnPress, OnPressDown, OnPressUp, OnChange,
and OnUpdate.

Provides script accessible events: OnPressEvent, OnPressDownEvent,
OnPressUpEvent, OnChangeEvent, and OnUpdateEvent.

####
[SteamVR_Behaviour_BooleanEvent](Valve.VR.SteamVR_Behaviour_BooleanEvent.html)

#### [SteamVR_Behaviour_Pose](Valve.VR.SteamVR_Behaviour_Pose.html)

This component simplifies the use of Pose actions. Adding it to a gameobject
will auto set that transform's position and rotation every update to match the
pose. Advanced velocity estimation is handled through a buffer of the last 30
updates.

about. You can set the transforms you're concerned with and ignore the ones
you're not.

####
[SteamVR_Skeleton_Poser.PoseBlendingBehaviour](Valve.VR.SteamVR_Skeleton_Poser.PoseBlendingBehaviour.html)

A filter applied to the base pose. Blends to a secondary pose by a certain
weight. Can be masked per-finger

####
[SteamVR_Skeleton_Poser.SkeletonBlendablePose](Valve.VR.SteamVR_Skeleton_Poser.SkeletonBlendablePose.html)

A SkeletonBlendablePose holds a reference to a Skeleton_Pose scriptableObject,
and also contains some helper functions. Also handles pose-specific animation
like additive finger motion.

####
[SteamVR_Skeleton_PoseSnapshot](Valve.VR.SteamVR_Skeleton_PoseSnapshot.html)

PoseSnapshots hold a skeleton pose for one hand, as well as storing which hand
they contain. They have several functions for combining BlendablePoses.

  * VRInputString_InputSource - What part of that controller is the origin. ex: "Trackpad".

#### skeletalTrackingLevel

Get the accuracy level of the skeletal tracking data.

* Estimated: Body part location can’t be directly determined by the device. Any skeletal pose provided by the device is estimated based on the active buttons, triggers, joysticks, or other input sensors. Examples include the Vive Controller and gamepads. 

* Partial: Body part location can be measured directly but with fewer degrees of freedom than the actual body part.Certain body part positions may be unmeasured by the device and estimated from other input data.Examples include Knuckles or gloves that only measure finger curl 

* Full: Body part location can be measured directly throughout the entire range of motion of the body part.Examples include hi-end mocap systems, or gloves that measure the rotation of each finger segment. 

##### Declaration

    
    
    EVRSkeletalTrackingLevel skeletalTrackingLevel { get; }

##### Property Value

Type | Description  
---|---  
[EVRSkeletalTrackingLevel](Valve.VR.EVRSkeletalTrackingLevel.html) |   
  
#### skeletalTransformSpace

The space to get bone data in. Parent space by default

##### Declaration

    
    
    EVRSkeletalTransformSpace skeletalTransformSpace { get; set; }

##### Property Value

Type | Description  
---|---  
[EVRSkeletalTransformSpace](Valve.VR.EVRSkeletalTransformSpace.html) |   
  
#### thumbCurl

A 0-1 value representing how curled the thumb is. 0 being straight, 1 being

Trigger the haptics at a certain time for a certain length

##### Declaration

    
    
    void Execute(float secondsFromNow, float durationSeconds, float frequency, float amplitude, SteamVR_Input_Sources inputSource)

##### Parameters

Type | Name | Description  
---|---|---  
System.Single | secondsFromNow | How long from the current time to execute the action (in seconds - can be 0)  
System.Single | durationSeconds | How long the haptic action should last (in seconds)  
System.Single | frequency | How often the haptic motor should bounce (0 - 320 in hz. The lower end being more useful)  
System.Single | amplitude | How intense the haptic action should be (0 - 1)  
[SteamVR_Input_Sources](Valve.VR.SteamVR_Input_Sources.html) | inputSource | The device you would like to execute the haptic action. Any if the action is not device specific.

# Enum SkeletalMotionRangeChange  
  
The change in range of the motion of the bones in the skeleton. Options are
"With Controller" as if your hand is holding your VR controller. Or "Without
Controller" as if your hand is empty.

###### **Namespace** : [Valve.VR](Valve.VR.html)

###### **Assembly** : Assembly-CSharp.dll

##### Syntax

    
    
    public enum SkeletalMotionRangeChange

### Fields

Name | Description  
---|---  
None |   
WithController | Estimation of bones in hand while holding a controller  
WithoutController | Estimation of bones in hand while hand is empty (allowing full fist)

  * VRInputString_Hand - Which hand the origin is in. ex: "Left Hand". 
  * VRInputString_ControllerType - What kind of controller the user has in that hand. ex: "Vive Controller". 
  * VRInputString_InputSource - What part of that controller is the origin. ex: "Trackpad".

#### skeletalTrackingLevel

Get the accuracy level of the skeletal tracking data.

* Estimated: Body part location can’t be directly determined by the device. Any skeletal pose provided by the device is estimated based on the active buttons, triggers, joysticks, or other input sensors. Examples include the Vive Controller and gamepads. 

* Partial: Body part location can be measured directly but with fewer degrees of freedom than the actual body part.Certain body part positions may be unmeasured by the device and estimated from other input data.Examples include Knuckles or gloves that only measure finger curl 

* Full: Body part location can be measured directly throughout the entire range of motion of the body part.Examples include hi-end mocap systems, or gloves that measure the rotation of each finger segment. 

##### Declaration

    
    
    public EVRSkeletalTrackingLevel skeletalTrackingLevel { get; }

Type | Description

[EVRSkeletalTrackingLevel](Valve.VR.EVRSkeletalTrackingLevel.html) |

##### Parameters

Type | Name | Description  
---|---|---  
[EVRInputStringBits](Valve.VR.EVRInputStringBits.html)[] | localizedParts | 

  * VRInputString_Hand - Which hand the origin is in. ex: "Left Hand". 
  * VRInputString_ControllerType - What kind of controller the user has in that hand. ex: "Vive Controller". 
  * VRInputString_InputSource - What part of that controller is the origin. ex: "Trackpad". 
  * VRInputString_All - All of the above. ex: "Left Hand Vive Controller Trackpad".

# Class SteamVR_Action_Skeleton_Source  
  
Skeleton Actions are our best approximation of where your hands are while
holding vr controllers and pressing buttons. We give you 31 bones to help you
animate hand models. For more information check out this blog post:
<https://steamcommunity.com/games/250820/announcements/detail/1690421280625220068>

#### skeletalTrackingLevel

Get the accuracy level of the skeletal tracking data.

* Estimated: Body part location can’t be directly determined by the device. Any skeletal pose provided by the device is estimated based on the active buttons, triggers, joysticks, or other input sensors. Examples include the Vive Controller and gamepads. 

* Partial: Body part location can be measured directly but with fewer degrees of freedom than the actual body part.Certain body part positions may be unmeasured by the device and estimated from other input data.Examples include Knuckles or gloves that only measure finger curl 

* Full: Body part location can be measured directly throughout the entire range of motion of the body part.Examples include hi-end mocap systems, or gloves that measure the rotation of each finger segment. 

##### Declaration

    
    
    public EVRSkeletalTrackingLevel skeletalTrackingLevel { get; }

[EVRSkeletalTrackingLevel](Valve.VR.EVRSkeletalTrackingLevel.html) |

## 📄 SOURCE: https://valvesoftware.github.io/steamvr_unity_plugin/api/Valve.VR.SteamVR_Behaviour_Boolean.html

# Class SteamVR_Behaviour_Boolean

This component simplifies using boolean actions.

Provides editor accessible events: OnPress, OnPressDown, OnPressUp, OnChange,
and OnUpdate.

Provides script accessible events: OnPressEvent, OnPressDownEvent,
OnPressUpEvent, OnChangeEvent, and OnUpdateEvent.

# Class SteamVR_Behaviour_Pose

This component simplifies the use of Pose actions. Adding it to a gameobject
will auto set that transform's position and rotation every update to match the
pose. Advanced velocity estimation is handled through a buffer of the last 30
updates.

  * VRInputString_Hand - Which hand the origin is in. E.g. "Left Hand"
  * VRInputString_ControllerType - What kind of controller the user has in that hand.E.g. "Vive Controller"
  * VRInputString_InputSource - What part of that controller is the origin. E.g. "Trackpad"
  * VRInputString_All - All of the above. E.g. "Left Hand Vive Controller Trackpad"

#### skeletalTrackingLevel

Get the accuracy level of the skeletal tracking data.

* Estimated: Body part location can’t be directly determined by the device. Any skeletal pose provided by the device is estimated based on the active buttons, triggers, joysticks, or other input sensors. Examples include the Vive Controller and gamepads. 

* Partial: Body part location can be measured directly but with fewer degrees of freedom than the actual body part.Certain body part positions may be unmeasured by the device and estimated from other input data.Examples include Knuckles or gloves that only measure finger curl 

* Full: Body part location can be measured directly throughout the entire range of motion of the body part.Examples include hi-end mocap systems, or gloves that measure the rotation of each finger segment. 

##### Declaration

    
    
    public EVRSkeletalTrackingLevel skeletalTrackingLevel { get; }

Type | Description

[EVRSkeletalTrackingLevel](Valve.VR.EVRSkeletalTrackingLevel.html) |

# Class SteamVR_Behaviour_SkeletonCustom

The major difference between this component and the standard
SteamVR_Behaviour_Skeleton is this one lets you only use the joints you care
about. You can set the transforms you're concerned with and ignore the ones
you're not.

  * VRInputString_ControllerType - What kind of controller the user has in that hand.E.g. "Vive Controller"
  * VRInputString_InputSource - What part of that controller is the origin. E.g. "Trackpad"

---|---|---

[EVRInputStringBits](Valve.VR.EVRInputStringBits.html)[] | localizedParts | 

  * VRInputString_Hand - Which hand the origin is in. E.g. "Left Hand"
  * VRInputString_ControllerType - What kind of controller the user has in that hand.E.g. "Vive Controller"
  * VRInputString_InputSource - What part of that controller is the origin. E.g. "Trackpad"
  * VRInputString_All - All of the above. E.g. "Left Hand Vive Controller Trackpad"
